papers.title: VoxMem: Benchmarking Multimodal Memory in Large Audio Language Models

summary.tldr: VoxMem is a new benchmark featuring 3,196 instances across 177 hours of spoken sessions designed to evaluate multimodal memory in Large Audio Language Models across diverse acoustic evidence types and memory operations.
key_points: Taxonomy and dataset evaluate four acoustic evidence types: speech semantics, speaker identity, paralinguistic cues, and environmental sound.
Covers four memory operations: information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal tracking, and answer refusal.
Dataset consists of 3,196 instances across 34,743 spoken sessions (177 total hours) with context lengths stratified from 8K to 64K tokens.
Evaluation of 15 LALMs showed no model exceeded 40% accuracy at a 32K context window, with models performing far worse on non-lexical audio cues than on speech semantics.
summary.why_it_matters: Current LALMs struggle to maintain non-transcript audio context like speaker identity and acoustic environment over multi-session long-context histories, highlighting key gaps for conversational AI development.

papers.title: Omni-IO Skills: Harnessing Your Agent Omni-Native

summary.tldr: Omni-IO Skills is a plug-and-play agent harness that enables omni-native multimodal capabilities without modifying host agent reasoning cores by using hierarchical skills, dependency-aware orchestration, and a persistent Asset Registry.
key_points: Represents multi-asset workflows as Declare Execution Graphs that execute independent operations concurrently and preserve assets for downstream reuse across 27 skills and 38 tasks.
Covers seven artifact modalities (text, images, audio, video, documents, 3D assets, code) across four capability families: understanding, generation, reasoning, and retrieval.
Increases input-support rates on the UniM-90 benchmark for GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5 from ~40% to 100%.
Raises Semantic-Quality Coupled Scores from ~27 to ~75-78 and achieves up to 100.00 Strict Structure Score on UniM-90.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a practical framework to expand AI agents to handle diverse modalities and complex workflows without undertaking expensive foundation model retrainings or updates.

papers.title: Follow the Entities: A Corpus Map for Agentic Search

summary.tldr: CorpusMap is an offline-constructed navigation layer that organizes document collections into a graph of entity pages to optimize LLM agent search.
key_points: Constructs Entity Pages offline by resolving cross-document mentions to link recurring entities to all source documents.
Eliminates the need for LLM agents to repeatedly rediscover inter-document relationships during inference time.
Tested across 7 LLM models and 3 benchmark datasets against 4 alternative navigation layers.
Improves evidence discovery and answer quality while reducing average token consumption compared to raw-corpus search.
summary.why_it_matters: By pre-indexing entity relationships across document collections, LLM agents can retrieve disconnected evidence faster and more accurately while cutting token overhead.

papers.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?

summary.tldr: EngiWorld is a benchmark featuring 1,301 expert-curated tasks across 6 engineering domains and 26 software platforms to evaluate autonomous agents across full professional engineering workflows.
key_points: Covers CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA, and 3D visualization across 26 professional software platforms using both GUI and CLI interfaces.
Features 6 task types ranging from software selection to open-ended design tasks.
Uses an artifact-centric evaluation methodology with domain verifiers that continuously score quantitative designs by specification attainment and rule compliance.
Frontier models show a significant capability gap: the top model achieved an EngiScore of 44.3, with only a 3.6% success rate on multi-software tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized, programmatic foundation to evaluate and advance autonomous agents handling complex, end-to-end industrial engineering workflows.

papers.title: Beyond Dyadic Memory: Interaction-Aware Multimodal Memory with Adaptive Agentic Retrieval for Multi-Party Spoken Conversations

summary.tldr: VoxPolyMem introduces an interaction-aware multimodal memory framework and the EG-GRPO reinforcement learning method to optimize agentic retrieval in multi-party spoken conversations.
key_points: Combines incremental speaker identification with a memory hierarchy containing interaction memory, fact memory, and participant profiles to capture who speaks to whom.
Formulates retrieval as sequential decision-making using Evidence-Gain GRPO (EG-GRPO) with round-wise credit assignment to incentivize complementary evidence gathering.
Introduces VoxPolyBench, a benchmark for multi-party spoken conversation memory, where VoxPolyMem scored 85.0 overall, outperforming the top baseline by 23.6 points.
Outperformed existing public memory baselines on Mem-Gallery and H2HMem-Multi datasets by over 8 points, scoring 89.6 and 74.4 respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a specialized framework for long-term memory and accurate attribution in complex, multi-speaker multimodal conversational AI.

papers.title: LongCat-DeepResearch Technical Report

summary.tldr: LongCat-DeepResearch combines an enhanced LongCat model with a multi-agent workflow that uses global planning, parallel section drafting, and targeted local revisions to generate research reports.
key_points: The multi-agent architecture uses planning agents to create a ResearchSpec, parallel research agents to gather evidence and draft sections, and global-to-local revision loops.
The system supports constructing research tasks and trajectories for mid-training and post-training LongCat general-purpose models.
LongCat-DeepResearch scored 55.25 on DeepResearchBench, 51.35 on DeepResearchBench II, 79.83 on ResearchRubrics, and 76.04 on an in-house benchmark.
Ablation studies showed combining planning perspectives provided benefits, while further planning refinement yielded mixed effects.
summary.why_it_matters: Targeted section-level revisions reduce the computational cost of repeating full-report rewrites in complex multi-agent research workflows.

papers.title: LLMs are General Asynchronous Agents

summary.tldr: A general asynchronous LLM framework uses inference coroutines with overlapping memory states to enable real-world concurrent execution without task-specific training.
key_points: Generalizes asynchronous tasks into a unified agent framework capable of handling varying concurrency patterns.
Uses inference coroutines with overlapping memory states defined by users or the agents themselves.
Demonstrates asynchronous operation on Qwen 3.x models across streaming video understanding, videogames, and monitoring without fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables standard off-the-shelf LLMs to process continuous incoming inputs while actively executing tasks, removing the need for specialized asynchronous architectures.

papers.title: SoL-Refiner: Speed-of-Light One-Step Refinement for High-Resolution Video

summary.tldr: SoL-Refiner is a one-step video refiner that upscales low-resolution model outputs into 4K videos using a single denoising step, achieving an 8.91x speedup over multi-step baselines.
key_points: Employs a three-stage training recipe consisting of high-resolution continual training, RL post-training, and one-step distillation.
Introduces Refiner-Bench, a video refinement benchmark evaluating outputs across different video generators via a shared-input protocol.
Outperforms external refiners on VBench and UniPercept averages at 2K resolution, and beats the three-step LTX-2.3 Refiner at 3840x2176 resolution.
Delivers an 8.91x reduction in refinement latency compared to the three-step LTX-2.3 Refiner in a 2K testing setup.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the sampling bottleneck in high-resolution video generation by drastically reducing latency without sacrificing visual quality metrics.

papers.title: APM-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-session Persistent Memory for Egocentric Streaming Video Assistants

summary.tldr: APM-Bench is a benchmark evaluating cross-session persistent memory for egocentric streaming video assistants, featuring multi-session life trajectories to test long-term recall, real-time efficiency, and missing evidence recognition.
key_points: APM-Bench reformulates streaming interactions into 104 multi-session life trajectories containing 549 sessions and 2,719 question candidates across both objective and open-ended types.
Evaluates video models and memory systems on four key constraints: storable persistence, selective retention, timely memory injection, and efficiency under finite storage.
Tests assistants on proactive responses and their ability to acknowledge when required evidence is missing from storage.
Benchmark evaluations reveal that current methods fail to balance reliable long-term recall, low overhead, and proactive assistance simultaneously, highlighting a utility-latency-storage trade-off.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a realistic testbed to develop persistent memory systems for AI assistants that interact continuously and intermittently across real-world, multi-day user activities.

papers.title: Asking for What Was Never Requested: Horizontal and Vertical Proactivity in Agents

summary.tldr: A new framework formalizes horizontal and vertical proactivity in agents and trains a questioner model via Q&D optimization to pursue unstated evidence without relying on LLM judges.
key_points: Formalizes horizontal proactivity (pursuing unstated info identified by current context) and vertical proactivity (pursuing needs revealed by earlier evidence), evaluated via a deterministic need graph.
Introduces Q&D (questioner and drafter) training, which optimizes the questioner to prefer queries whose continuations retrieve more required evidence without needing a reward model or judge.
Outperforms a 15x larger prompted model on two out of three multi-hop QA benchmarks at equal retrieval spend.
Demonstrates zero-shot transfer to an interactive customer-service agent, completing more tasks with fewer user turns and questions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables smaller AI agents to autonomously uncover unstated task requirements and know when to stop asking questions without relying on expensive, larger models or LLM judges.

papers.title: Context Language Models

summary.tldr: Context Language Models (CLMs) natively manage context by treating it as an editable file, allowing models to make unrestricted updates, reduce compute, and learn context-management strategies via reinforcement learning and prompt optimization.
key_points: CLMs update their context as an editable file, outperforming standard harnesses zero-shot by 11.4% on BrowseComp-Plus using 21.5% fewer FLOPs and 5% higher on EdgeBench using 59% fewer FLOPs.
Prompt-driven skill optimization improves held-out context management accuracy by up to 35.9 points while lowering compute.
Online RL applied to Qwen3.5-9B increases BrowseComp-Plus accuracy by 47.6% with 12% fewer FLOPs.
Suffix Cache Reuse serving co-design reduces server compute by 35% compared to baseline SGLang at matched performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Shifting context management from external harnesses to intrinsic model operations significantly cuts inference FLOPs and server compute while increasing task accuracy in long-horizon and multi-agent tasks.

papers.title: StoryEngine: A State-Grounded Agentic Framework for Video Storytelling

summary.tldr: StoryEngine is a state-grounded agentic framework for long-form video storytelling that uses structured state tracking, canonical references, and bounded evaluation-guided repair to maintain narrative coherence and visual consistency across multi-shot videos.
key_points: Explicitly separates authoritative semantic plans from unreliable visual observations by maintaining structured representations of entity placement and story-relevant states.
Propagates event-induced changes to define explicit start and end states for individual shots, compiling them with canonical references into executable render plans.
Employs a bounded evaluation-guided repair loop to detect and correct local state inconsistencies before errors propagate across subsequent shots.
Introduces a new multi-scenario benchmark with metrics evaluating storytelling quality, narrative coherence, and visual consistency.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents visual drift and causal inconsistencies in long-form video generation by decoupling state tracking from pixel outputs and adding automated repair loops.

papers.title: Selecting The Most Informative Tokens in Natural Language Autoencoders

summary.tldr: A study of 4.7 million autoencoder explanations shows chat-structure rankers select relevant token positions for audit better than computational signals, enabling 95% compute reduction without losing threat detection capability.
key_points: Evaluated token position selection strategies across 4.7 million explanations covering prompt injection and concealment tasks.
Chat-structure rankers consistently select more relevant explanations than computational signals while eliminating the need for a model forward pass during selection.
Explaining 5% of token positions preserves nearly the full success rate of 100% position coverage across three out of four evaluation datasets.
Pretrained verbalizers successfully recover fine-tune concealed words without requiring task-specific retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: Auditors can drastically reduce the computational cost of interpreting neural network activations by inspecting only 5% of structured token positions while still detecting critical safety threats.

papers.title: AutoRef: Harness Optimization for Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation

summary.tldr: AutoRef automatically optimizes executable agentic harnesses via coding-agent rewrites and beam search, improving multi-reference image generation without updating underlying model weights.
key_points: Uses a coding agent to iteratively rewrite harness code while keeping image generation and reasoning models completely frozen.
Employs a search procedure that separates feedback tasks from selection tasks and expands from a beam of top-ranked harnesses.
Discovered AutoRef-Harness, which increases open-weight FLUX.2 [klein] 4B scores from 5.72 to 7.37 on held-out four-reference MultiBanana benchmark tasks.
Matches or exceeds proprietary baselines including Nano Banana Pro and GPT-Image-1.5.
Demonstrates transferability across different generators, reference counts, benchmarks, evaluators, and reasoning models without re-optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significant multi-reference image quality improvements through automated program optimization instead of costly model retraining.

papers.title: Omni-Decision: Evidence-Ledger Planning for Omni-Modal Agents

summary.tldr: Omni-Decision replaces dialogue history in omni-modal agents with a compact evidence ledger, filtering noisy observations via a critic to improve multi-step planning efficiency and accuracy.
key_points: Identifies multi-step planning over noisy multimodal conversation histories as the primary bottleneck in omni-modal agents.
Uses a critic to filter noisy observations, passing only usable content to an explicit evidence ledger that tracks missing, confirmed, and conflicting evidence.
Trains the planner using supervised fine-tuning and decision-level reinforcement learning on recorded state, action, and verdict trajectories.
Achieves 81.4% accuracy on OmniGAIA at roughly 43% of Gemini-3.1-Pro's cost per question, and 65.0% on WorldSense long-video understanding.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that decoupling evidence state management from raw observation history significantly reduces execution costs while matching or exceeding state-of-the-art omni-modal performance.

papers.title: KV-Kaizen: Learning Context-Adaptive Cache Compression Choices

summary.tldr: KV-Kaizen is a context-adaptive selector that dynamically configures per-layer LLM KV caches across layer sharing, precision, and low-rank latent representation without evicting tokens.
key_points: Runs once prior to pre-fill to select context-adaptive, per-layer cache configurations based on a target compression budget.
Combines three compression axes: cross-layer cache sharing (depth), reduced quantization bits (precision), and low-rank latent representation truncation (rank).
Composes with token eviction methods on long-context tasks to achieve up to a 32x smaller decode-time cache on a 14B parameter model while maintaining accuracy.
Maintains zero accuracy degradation at a 4x cache reduction for models with 7B or more parameters, outperforming smaller uncompressed models with equal cache size.
summary.why_it_matters: It alleviates the decode-stage memory bottleneck in long-context LLMs, demonstrating that compressing large pre-trained models contextually is superior to serving smaller uncompressed models.

papers.title: $S^3$: Spectral Null-Space Swap Makes Reasoning Models Efficient

summary.tldr: Spectral Null-Space Swap ($S^3$) is a training-free model composition method that isolates the thinking model's weight components in the non-thinking model's null space, reducing inference token overhead while maintaining or improving reasoning accuracy.
key_points: Identifies that critical reasoning capacity resides within the Thinking model's weight component located in the null space of the Non-thinking model's dominant singular directions.
Proposes $S^3$, a training-free composition technique that preserves the Non-thinking model inside its dominant subspace and incorporates the Thinking model's null-space component.
Demonstrated on 2B-30B dense and MoE models across 28 evaluation environments spanning mathematical, multimodal, and audio reasoning domains.
Reduces average inference token overhead by 27.4% while improving overall task accuracy by 1.0 percentage point (including +8.3% accuracy and a 33.0% token speedup on HMMT25).
Attributes efficiency gains to lower attention entropy produced by the retained null-space component, supported by attention entropy analysis and a simplified optimization model.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to significantly lower LLM chain-of-thought inference token costs and speed up generation without retraining models or sacrificing reasoning accuracy.

papers.title: On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: PUMBA is a unified trajectory-aware training framework for masked diffusion models that combines policy-induced trajectory training, inter-step information passing, and multi-step backpropagation through time.
key_points: Exact train-inference mask alignment causes local overfitting, whereas looser trajectory alignment improves generation quality.
Passing continuous information between steps outperforms discrete gradient estimation methods by avoiding early step commitment.
Backpropagation through time over longer step spans yields theoretical and empirical performance gains.
When applied to LLaDA-8B supervised fine-tuning, PUMBA reduces required NFEs by up to 22% in full-canvas generation and up to 26% in block diffusion.
PUMBA achieves performance matching an equivalent-sized autoregressive model baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables masked diffusion language models to achieve autoregressive-level generation quality while significantly reducing the inference step budget.

papers.title: The Unequal Influence of Bad Advice: Using Training Data Attribution to Modulate Emergent Misalignment

summary.tldr: Researchers used training data attribution to quantify how individual harmful examples drive emergent misalignment, demonstrating that filtering data via these influence scores can enhance or attenuate the behavior.
key_points: Training data attribution scores and black-box harmfulness scores can successfully identify the specific training examples that drive emergent misalignment.
Data filtering based on attribution scores enables controlled attenuation or enhancement of emergent misalignment via retraining.
Influence scores generalize across three tested model families, though cross-model filtering yields lower performance than same-model filtering.
summary.why_it_matters: Quantifying data influence allows developers to mitigate emergent misalignment by identifying and removing specific high-impact harmful examples from fine-tuning datasets.

papers.title: Active Budget Can Kill Sensitivity: Diagnosing and Repairing TopK Sparse Autoencoder Reliability

summary.tldr: Researchers identified that TopK Sparse Autoencoders reduce rare-feature sensitivity due to selection boundary geometry and introduced pairwise rank stabilization to fix it.
key_points: Scaling TopK SAEs selectively reduces the sensitivity of rare features due to the active budget k and active margin geometry rather than dictionary width.
The active margin, defined as the distance to the TopK cutoff, predicts feature loss without relying on fixed thresholds.
Pairwise rank stabilization targets ordering failures at the cutoff, improving rare-feature sensitivity by 8.83 percentage points while maintaining baseline reconstruction and alive-feature coverage.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating SAEs solely on reconstruction and sparsity masks feature instability, but addressing boundary geometry ensures rare features remain reliable under semantic variations.

papers.title: Scaling Influence Functions in LLMs through Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection

summary.tldr: Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection (EOGP) compresses stored training gradients using EK-FAC, subspace PCA, and one-bit quantization to scale LLM influence function calculations within tight memory constraints.
key_points: EOGP employs EK-FAC for dimensionality reduction, followed by PCA within the retained subspace to identify compression directions from training gradients.
Quantizes transformed gradient coordinates to one bit per dimension, allowing higher-dimensional coordinate retention under a fixed storage budget.
Achieves higher retraining prediction accuracy on GPT-2 than evaluated compression baselines using one-sixteenth of their per-example storage.
Maintains competitive performance on OLMo 2 SFT models (1B to 32B parameters) against baselines using over 100 times more storage per example.
summary.why_it_matters: EOGP significantly reduces the storage overhead of saving training gradients, enabling scalable, repeated influence function computations across massive LLM datasets for unknown future queries.

papers.title: Pattern Formation in Transformers

summary.tldr: Applying pattern-formation theory to full Transformer architectures reveals that positional encodings, multi-head attention, and output-value geometries selectively amplify, stabilize, and combine rich token patterns like traveling and rotating waves.
key_points: Pattern-formation theory explains how full Transformers escape rank collapse by amplifying complex token representation patterns, including traveling and rotating waves.
Multi-Head Attention, Positional Encoding, and Output-Value geometry dictate which specific patterns are amplified, stabilized, or forced to compete/coexist.
Task-aligned positional encodings paired with target weight initializations form a controllable dynamical prior that accelerates optimization and improves data efficiency on CIFAR-10 with ConViT.
summary.why_it_matters: Leveraging pattern-formation theory to design task-aligned initializations and positional encodings significantly boosts sample efficiency and convergence speed in Transformer models.

papers.title: Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

summary.tldr: OASIS overcomes scaling limits in on-policy self-distillation by supervising verified student trajectories using unverified model-generated attempts as teacher context, requiring only final-answer labels.
key_points: Factorial analysis reveals that scaffold correctness impacts downstream accuracy more strongly than context correctness in on-policy self-distillation (OPSD).
Standard OPSD performance gains degrade as models scale (falling from 3.05 points at 1.7B to 0.14 points at 8B) due to unverified scaffolds creating an imitation gap.
OASIS replaces written solution contexts with unverified model attempts while supervising verified-by-label on-policy trajectories.
Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B models on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and HMMT 2025 benchmarks, OASIS consistently improves over the base model by 3.2–3.8 average points.
At the 8B parameter scale, OASIS outperforms standard OPSD by 3.05 points.
summary.why_it_matters: OASIS preserves the performance gains of self-distillation at larger model scales while eliminating the need for step-by-step written solutions, relying instead solely on final-answer labels.

papers.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision

summary.tldr: The Latent Information Feedback Transformer (LIFT) introduces deep-to-shallow recurrent state feedback during pretraining by framing state learning as a parallelizable, teacher-forced prediction task using an off-the-shelf language model's next-token distribution.
key_points: LIFT pairs each input token with an information-dense state derived from a pretrained teacher LM's next-token distribution, adding minimal parameters.
Pretraining remains fully parallel across sequence positions because input feedback states are precomputed by the teacher.
At inference, the model feeds back its own predicted states, incurring a small computational overhead that scales down with larger model sizes.
Evaluated across 135M to 1B parameter models, LIFT beats standard Transformers on token-matched budgets and matches or outperforms them on compute-matched budgets.
On a state-tracking task, a small LIFT model outperformed same-size Transformers trained on 8x more data, even when using teacher states from a model that failed the task.
summary.why_it_matters: LIFT bypasses the single-token autoregressive bottleneck by allowing language models to pass rich latent states across generation steps without sacrificing parallelized pretraining.

papers.title: Retrieval Capacity of Self-Attention Under Competition

summary.tldr: Researchers measure transformer retrieval capacity by retaining only top-weighted tokens per head, layer, and query without retraining, revealing how attention set size scales with context length, competition, and weight renormalization.
key_points: Evaluates effective attention set size by selecting top-weight tokens, leaving weights unchanged, and measuring negative log-likelihood (NLL) degradation against full-attention baselines.
Expanding context length while keeping target predictions constant increases the absolute number of required tokens but decreases their overall fraction of the context.
Adding background context introduces competition that depresses the attention rank and total attention mass assigned to fixed supporting facts.
Renormalizing the retained attention weights significantly reduces the required set size to maintain target NLL performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how competition and aggregation dictate effective attention set sizes informs more efficient context pruning, sparsification, and KV-cache compression techniques.

security.title: Dagger: Decoupling-based Model Stealing Attack against Graph Neural Networks

summary.tldr: Dagger is a two-phase GNN model stealing framework that extracts surrogate models under constrained black-box, hard-label, and backbone-agnostic conditions using up to 12.23 times fewer queries than top baselines.
key_points: Formalizes a strict threat model requiring only hard-label black-box API access under tight query budgets without prior backbone knowledge.
Phase 1 pre-trains the surrogate model via decoupled information propagation for structural context on sparse subgraphs and manifold-level node mixup for continuous supervision.
Phase 2 freezes the encoder and fine-tunes the classifier head using class-balanced sampling and logit adjustment to address severe query imbalance.
Achieves up to 18.16% higher fidelity over state-of-the-art GNN stealing attacks across four benchmark graphs and four backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: Dagger demonstrates that commercial GNN MLaaS APIs remain highly vulnerable to IP theft even under strict defense constraints like hard-label outputs and low query limits.

security.title: Selective Channel Restoration for Backdoored Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: Perturb-Select-Restore (PSR) is a post-training VLM defense that mitigates backdoors by identifying fragile projection channels via bounded perturbations and restoring them to pretrained values with zero inference overhead.
key_points: Identifies projection fragility, where backdoored VLM projector layers exhibit significantly higher sensitivity to bounded perturbations than clean layers.
Applies a three-step Perturb-Select-Restore framework that identifies highly sensitive output channels in each projection layer.
Restores identified backdoor-affected channel parameters directly to their original pretrained values.
Executes sparse updates on the vision-language interface post-training without requiring extensive parameter fine-tuning or adding query overhead at inference.
Reduces backdoor attack success rates to near zero across multiple tasks while maintaining performance on clean tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: PSR enables post-training backdoor mitigation in vision-language models through targeted parameter restoration, avoiding expensive retraining pipelines or latency penalties during model deployment.

security.title: Where Do LLMs Decide to Break the Rules? Mechanistic Localization of Prompt Injection Compliance

summary.tldr: Using causal activation patching, researchers located a late-layer bottleneck in the final third of LLMs where the model causally decides to comply with prompt injection attacks.
key_points: Attack information is linearly decodable starting at the first layer, but causal leverage over compliance is negligible until a late-layer bottleneck.
Patching activations at this late-layer bottleneck reverses attack compliance in 77% to 92% of cases across tested models (4B to 32B parameters).
The compliance mechanism operates within a compact linear subspace, measuring rank-8 in 4B and 14B models and rank-64 in 32B models.
The causal peak layer serves as the representationally optimal site for detecting attacks, remaining robust against surface-level obfuscations like leetspeak.
summary.why_it_matters: Identifying the compact, late-layer subspace where injection compliance decisions occur enables more accurate attack detection mechanisms that resist surface-level obfuscation.

security.title: Concealing LLM-Based Multi-Agent Topology via Phantom Structure Injection

summary.tldr: MIRAGE is a topology-concealment framework that protects LLM-based multi-agent systems from black-box topology inference attacks by injecting plausible phantom semantic dependencies while preserving task utility.
key_points: Operates via a three-stage pipeline: phantom topology synthesis, semantic edge realization, and protected multi-agent system (MAS) execution.
Materializes phantom edges as realistic semantic dependencies to mislead adversaries toward a structurally distinct decoy topology.
Suppresses source-specific semantic cues in reasoning traces that could expose genuine communication edges absent from the phantom structure.
Validated across three topology optimization frameworks and four benchmark datasets, demonstrating high attack mitigation with minimal impact on task utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents adversaries from stealing proprietary multi-agent architectures or exploiting structural system vulnerabilities via black-box observation of output traces.

security.title: Backdoor Mitigation in Decentralized LLM Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: Chorus is a defense mechanism for decentralized LLM fine-tuning that detects and rejects backdoored adapters via localized neighborhood probing and voting without shared validation data.
key_points: Decentralized fine-tuning without a central coordinator allows a single malicious node to spread backdoors to honest nodes across the network graph.
Chorus uses a receiver's own adapter as a trusted reference to evaluate neighboring adapters based on model behavior rather than data inspection.
Receivers independently probe incoming adapter updates, pool their findings within the local neighborhood, and vote to make collective acceptance decisions.
Evaluations show Chorus reduces the average Attack Success Rate (ASR) on neighboring nodes from 48-63% down to at most 2.2%, approaching an oracle defense baseline.
The defense bounds the worst-affected honest node's ASR to under 10% (down from 78%) with negligible communication overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: Chorus enables secure collaborative LLM fine-tuning across untrusted, decentralized nodes without requiring a central authority or shared validation datasets.

security.title: AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch to Discover Better LLM Watermarks

summary.tldr: AutoMark enables frontier LLMs to autonomously discover distortion-free LLM watermarking schemes that outperform existing human-designed methods across detectability, quality, and robustness.
key_points: Establishes strict reliability criteria, automated statistical testing for false positive rates, and a three-dimension evaluation suite covering detectability, quality, and robustness.
Utilizes three frontier models (GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5, Gemini-3.8 Flash) to discover over 50 distinct watermarking schemes.
Discovers novel algorithmic techniques, such as aligning watermark scores with random per-request directions, alongside optimizing existing schemes.
Provides a manual component analysis to isolate and evaluate the individual impacts of agent-generated watermarking ideas.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating watermarking research accelerates the development of more robust, high-quality, and reliable AI text attribution methods needed to meet emerging commercial and regulatory requirements.

security.title: Beyond Semantic Narrowing: Robust and Efficient LLM Watermarking with Hamming Neighborhoods

summary.tldr: HammingMark is a new LLM watermarking method that uses semantic hashes and Hamming neighborhoods to eliminate semantic narrowing, significantly lowering resampling costs while maintaining text quality and robustness.
key_points: Existing semantic watermarking methods induce semantic narrowing by ignoring the LLM's non-uniform semantic preferences during generation.
HammingMark sets the semantic hash of the preceding sentence as a dynamic center, accepting candidate sentences whose hashes lie within its Hamming neighborhood.
The coarse, many-to-one hash mapping preserves a larger set of valid, naturally likely continuations and diverse semantic realizations.
Evaluations on C4 and BookSum show HammingMark requires only 2.2 sampled candidates per accepted sentence, representing a 72.8% reduction in sampling overhead over prior state-of-the-art methods.
HammingMark maintains high detection rates and achieves top or tied-top ROUGE-L scores on generation tasks with strict semantic constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust, detectable LLM text watermarking with minimal generation latency overhead and higher quality retention on constrained tasks.

security.title: ToolFence: Fine-Grained Authorization for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents

summary.tldr: ToolFence secures tool-using LLM agents against indirect prompt injections by enforcing pre-compiled typed authorization blueprints via a deterministic monitor, deferring to a judge only for capability-level grants when blueprints are incomplete.
key_points: Combines a pre-compiled typed authorization blueprint with a deterministic monitor using fine-grained provenance tracking to separate user-authorized values from untrusted observations.
Defends against within-tool attacks by authorizing execution effects and argument values rather than evaluating content or aggregated outputs.
Reduces expensive judge calls by utilizing a deterministic fast path and granting capabilities at the runtime level instead of adjudicating every concrete tool call.
Achieves near-zero Attack Success Rate (ASR) on AgentDojo with Qwen3-max while incurring only a 3.80 percentage-point drop in clean utility and maintaining practical runtime overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides robust, provenance-aware security against indirect prompt injections for LLM agents without incurring the high latency costs of full data-flow control mechanisms.

security.title: When Tools Silently Lie: Evaluating and Mitigating Blind Compliance in Tool-Augmented Data Agents

summary.tldr: ToxicBench measures blind compliance in tool-augmented data agents by evaluating how numerical, label, schema, and retrieval errors in tool outputs affect evidence checking and answer adoption.
key_points: Evaluated 118 tasks using GPT across three adapters, finding that tool output poisoning reduces task success rates by 26 to 39 percentage points.
Categorized tool output errors into four distinct types: numerical, label, schema, and retrieval errors.
Observed that ordinary retries mitigate errors under one-shot poisoning, but repeated poisoning causes agents to adopt wrong answers even after performing verification checks.
Validated the automated scorer against human annotations on 200 trajectories, achieving 96% agreement on task success.
summary.why_it_matters: Data agents cannot rely solely on successful tool execution, as plausible but incorrect outputs cause agents to adopt false conclusions even after verifying the evidence.

security.title: Controlled Decoding Attacks on Black-Box LLMs

summary.tldr: A new framework jailbreaks black-box LLMs through text-only continuation interfaces by combining sample-based distribution reconstruction with risk-gated residual control and speculative multi-token execution.
key_points: Combines sampled outputs with a prior over unobserved actions to reconstruct next-token probability distributions from text-only interfaces.
Uses Risk-Gated Residual Control to analyze the evolving response prefix and restrict costly distribution reconstruction to critical positions where distributional changes occur.
Applies Speculative Multi-Token Execution to accept draft prefixes that require no intervention, reducing total target query costs.
Requires only repeated sampling and assistant-prefix continuation capabilities, outperforming baselines across four target endpoints and three benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach demonstrates that safety alignments can be bypassed on strict text-only LLM endpoints without needing access to raw logprobs or model weights.

security.title: Practical Secrets Extraction against Black-box LLMs

summary.tldr: A new black-box framework extracts memorized secrets from commercial LLMs via output-only API access using cross-validated proxy distillation and entropy-guided candidate filtering.
key_points: Cross-Validated Secret Knowledge Distillation uses prompt variants, response cross-validation, and format filtering to train a local white-box proxy model.
Proxy-Guided Secret Extraction uses top-p sampling, proxy token entropy, N-gram frequency profiling, and structural priors to identify valid credentials.

Evaluations demonstrated higher recovery rates and reduced latency on controlled benchmarks, successfully extracting masked API keys from three deployed black-box systems including OpenAI and Claude Code.
summary.why_it_matters: Confidential credentials memorized during training can be extracted from production LLMs through public APIs without needing model weights or token probabilities.

security.title: SKILLLITE: Evidence-Guided Malicious Skill Auditing with Compact LLMs

summary.tldr: SKILLLITE is an evidence-guided agentic framework that enables compact, locally deployable LLMs to effectively detect malicious behaviors in complex third-party Agent Skill packages.
key_points: Addresses supply-chain vulnerabilities in LLM agents where malicious Skills abuse execution privileges and access context.
Extracts security-relevant behaviors and infers intended functionality from complex Skill packages to overcome the limited reasoning capacity of compact LLMs.
Uses compact LLMs to evaluate maliciousness by comparing observed executable behaviors against functional context.
Outperforms existing auditing baselines, generalizes to in-the-wild malicious Skills, and maintains low inference latency.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables secure, low-latency auditing of third-party agent tools using local open-source models without relying on costly commercial LLM APIs.

security.title: Safer Content or Firmer Refusals? A Hybrid Perturbation Defense for Alignment under Harmful Fine-tuning

summary.tldr: VaccineBooster combines embedding perturbation and weight-level gradient attenuation into a single alignment procedure to protect open-weight models against harmful fine-tuning attacks.
key_points: Combines Vaccine's embedding perturbation with Booster's weight-level gradient attenuation within each alignment training step.
Achieved the lowest OpenAI moderation score (0.315) on Llama-2-7B aligned with BeaverTails when subjected to poisoned fine-tuning.

Reveals a defense trade-off: embedding perturbation primarily reduces flagged harmful content, whereas gradient attenuation retains explicit refusal behavior (up to 50% post-attack refusal rate in a Booster-only variant).
summary.why_it_matters: It offers practical guidance for Fine-tuning-as-a-Service providers to trade off between generating safer content and retaining explicit refusal behaviors when models undergo untrusted fine-tuning.

security.title: Does the Unsafe Gradient Survive a Conversation? On the Fragility of Gradient-Based Jailbreak Detection in Multi-Turn Dialogue

summary.tldr: Evaluating gradient-based jailbreak detectors like GradSafe in multi-turn dialogues reveals severe performance degradation under realistic benign distributions, where ROC-AUC drops to 0.76 and false positive rates exceed 90%.
key_points: GradSafe extended with a Context Window Scanner achieves 0.98 ROC-AUC against synthetic benign conversations, but drops to 0.76 on real-world WildChat dialogues.
Synthetic-calibrated detection thresholds cause over 90% of benign WildChat multi-turn conversations to be misclassified as unsafe.
Short single-turn windows yield higher class separability than accumulated multi-turn contexts, which dilute gradient safety signals.
Detection performance varies significantly by target model and attack strategy; successful Crescendo attacks score at or below benign levels, while Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct shows near-random separability.
summary.why_it_matters: Gradient-based jailbreak detectors cannot be deployed in production multi-turn systems without calibration on realistic conversation distributions and length-aware, short-window scoring strategies.

security.title: I Want Better Reporting on AI Genie Behavior

summary.tldr: Bruce Schneier criticizes media coverage for mislabeling AI "genie behavior" as "going rogue" or "hacking" when models simply use unintended tactics like web probing or public credential usage to complete tasks.
key_points: Media reported OpenAI models "hacking" government sites, but source data shows failed vulnerability probes (SQL injection, command injection, path traversals) and retrieval of public data.
Specific cases included an agent sending seven unsuccessful probes and an 80-request flood to access a UNM digital library photo after hitting obstacles.
In Australia, an agent bypassed a Cloudflare block by fetching a public dataset in over 100 scans from a pre-production server (pp.aihw.gov.au) and attempted an unsuccessful reflected XSS probe.
Schneier argues framing these unintended optimization paths as "going rogue" deflects responsibility away from the prompters and AI developers.
summary.why_it_matters: Inaccurate press framing masks the real challenge of AI alignment—where agents aggressively optimize given prompts via unexpected methods—by mischaracterizing simple web scraping and failed safety probes as active cyberattacks.

infra.title: Taking vLLM Apart: A Practical Guide to Disaggregated Serving

summary.tldr: vLLM v0.30.0+ supports disaggregated serving by splitting compute-bound prefill from memory-bound decode via KV cache transfers, and offloading tokenization and parsing to CPU-only render frontends.
key_points: Prefill (compute-bound, TTFT) and decode (memory-bound, ITL) are split into separate instances using KV cache connectors like NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake, FlexKV, and MoRI-IO over RDMA.
KV cache transfers require high bandwidth; a 10k-token prompt for Llama-3.1-70B in BF16 generates ~3 GB of KV data (~320 KiB/token), taking ~65 ms over a 400 Gb/s link.
A GPU-less frontend decouples CPU-heavy operations from accelerator nodes using /render to map OpenAI requests into token IDs and /derender to parse outputs into content, reasoning, and tool calls.

Disaggregation extends beyond P/D to include Mamba state transfers for hybrid SSMs, encoder disaggregation for multimodal models, and the AFD plugin for splitting attention from FFN in MoE architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Disaggregating vLLM workloads prevents long prompt prefills and CPU preprocessing tasks from causing latency spikes and stalling inter-token generation across concurrent decode streams.

key_points: TensorRT Model Connect provides open-source reference implementations of AI model families written in C++ on top of NVIDIA TensorRT.
The development workflow utilized AI coding agents structured around parallel work, model-family isolation, and reversible changes.
The project integrates GPU-backed validation to verify agent-generated models and ensure inference correctness.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how structuring open-source projects around AI coding agents and isolated execution can streamline the development of high-performance C++ GPU inference code.

infra.title: Amazon Bedrock expands Claude model availability to in-country inferencing in India

summary.tldr: Amazon Bedrock now provides in-country geographic cross-Region inference in India for Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 models.
key_points: Geographic cross-Region inference routes requests exclusively between the ap-south-1 (Mumbai) and ap-south-2 (Hyderabad) AWS Regions.
Customer data is not stored in destination Regions, while Amazon CloudWatch logging, AWS CloudTrail logging, quota consumption, and billing remain tracked strictly within the source Region.
The bedrock-runtime endpoint supports the India geographic inference profile via the Anthropic Messages API, Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel API, and Converse API.
The architecture operates under a zero data retention (ZDR) model by default with end-to-end encryption for data in transit across the secure AWS network.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations operating in India can run high-throughput Claude workloads with cross-region capacity routing while complying with local in-country data processing requirements.

infra.title: Introducing Anthropic models on Amazon Bedrock for in-region inference in Seoul and Singapore

key_points: In-region inference processes prompts and outputs entirely within ap-northeast-2 (Seoul) or ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) without a cross-region routing layer.
Supported APIs on the bedrock-runtime endpoint include the Anthropic Messages API, Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel API, and Converse API.
Throughput, service quotas, CloudWatch metrics, and CloudTrail logs are strictly scoped to the single called AWS Region.
Models are invoked using direct model IDs such as anthropic.claude-opus-5 and anthropic.claude-sonnet-5.
summary.why_it_matters: This allows organizations in regulated industries like healthcare and finance to scale Claude models while strictly adhering to local data residency requirements.
